summary.text: Hagia Sophia is a mosque and major historical site in Istanbul, Turkey, that was a church from 360 to 1453 and a museum from 1935 to 2020.
The current building was built by the Byzantine emperor Justinian I between 532 and 537, designed by the geometers Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles.
When completed it was the world's largest interior space, and it is considered the epitome of Byzantine architecture.

items.prompt: In its cathedral, a papal envoy delivers a formal excommunication to the patriarch of Constantinople. What split in Christianity is this act considered to have started?

options.label: The Western Schism within the Catholic Church
The split caused by the Fourth Crusade
The East-West Schism
The Nika riots

items.explain: The excommunication of Patriarch Michael I Cerularius was delivered there by the envoy of Pope Leo IX in 1054, an act considered the start of the East-West Schism.

items.prompt: Crusaders led by the doge of Venice take Constantinople. What happens to the great cathedral of the Eastern Orthodox Church?

options.label: It becomes a Catholic cathedral until the Byzantines regain the city
It is left alone as an Orthodox cathedral
It is turned into a mosque under the Crusaders
It is torn down and its stone reused

items.explain: During the Fourth Crusade it was converted into a Catholic cathedral under the Latin Empire, and was restored to the Eastern Orthodox Church when the Byzantine Empire was restored.

items.prompt: A mosque built long after the Byzantine era copies features of Hagia Sophia. What does this show about the building?

options.label: It was first designed by Ottoman architects
It was a mosque from the start
It was copied only by its own city's churches
Its style became a model that others copied, even for mosques

items.explain: It became the quintessential model for Eastern Orthodox church architecture, and Ottoman mosques emulated its style a thousand years later.

items.prompt: Hagia Sophia was a museum for decades. What formally allowed it to be reclassified as a mosque in 2020?

options.label: A vote by the UNESCO world heritage committee
A Council of State ruling annulling the museum decision
The return of the Orthodox patriarch to the building
A fire that forced the museum to close for good

items.explain: The Council of State annulled the decision that had established the museum, and the building was reclassified as a mosque. The move was highly controversial, with UNESCO among those condemning it.

items.prompt: Justinian's Hagia Sophia was the third church of that name on the site. What happened to the one before it?

options.label: It was converted into a mosque
It was moved to a new site by Constantine
It was knocked down to build a palace
It was destroyed in the Nika riots

items.explain: The prior church had been destroyed in the Nika riots, and Justinian then had the current structure built between 532 and 537.

items.prompt: A visitor assumes Hagia Sophia is named after a saint called Sophia. What was the church actually dedicated to?

options.label: Holy Wisdom
Holy Peace
The Great Church
New Rome

items.explain: The church was dedicated to Holy Wisdom, and was formally called the Temple of God's Holy Wisdom. Holy Peace is the name of the nearby Hagia Irene.

paragraphs.heading: One building, many lives
paragraphs.text: Hagia Sophia stands in Istanbul and is today a mosque as well as one of Turkey's great historic sites. It has changed roles several times: a church from 360 to 1453, then a mosque, then a museum from 1935 to 2020, and a mosque again from 2020. Its formal Greek name meant the Temple of God's Holy Wisdom, and the church was dedicated to Holy Wisdom.

paragraphs.heading: Built by Justinian
paragraphs.text: The present building is the third church on the spot. The one before it was destroyed in the Nika riots, and the emperor Justinian I had the new one raised between 532 and 537. Its designers were two Greek geometers, Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles. When it was finished it held the largest interior space in the world.

paragraphs.heading: A model for later builders
paragraphs.text: Hagia Sophia was among the first buildings to use a fully pendentive dome. It is seen as the high point of Byzantine architecture, and it is said to have changed the history of architecture. No church on earth was bigger for more than five centuries, until Cluny's abbey church was completed in the 12th century. Eastern Orthodox churches took it as their model, and Ottoman mosques copied its style a thousand years later, among them the Süleymaniye Mosque.

paragraphs.heading: Heart of a church
paragraphs.text: For close to a thousand years it was the religious centre of the Eastern Orthodox Church and the seat of the ecumenical patriarch of Constantinople. In 1054 a papal envoy, Humbert of Silva Candida, delivered the excommunication of Patriarch Michael I Cerularius there. That act is taken as the start of the split between the Eastern and Western churches.

paragraphs.heading: Crusaders and sultans
paragraphs.text: During the Fourth Crusade in 1204 it became a Catholic cathedral, and it went back to the Orthodox Church when the Byzantine Empire returned in 1261. Enrico Dandolo, the Venetian doge who led that crusade, was buried inside. After the Ottomans took the city in 1453, Mehmed the Conqueror made it a mosque, and minarets were soon added. It served as Istanbul's main mosque until the Sultan Ahmed Mosque was built in 1616.

paragraphs.heading: Museum, then mosque again
paragraphs.text: The building closed to the public in 1931 and reopened four years later as a museum of the secular Turkish Republic. By 2019 it was the country's most visited tourist attraction. In 2020 Turkey's Council of State cancelled the 1934 decision behind the museum, and Hagia Sophia became a mosque once more. The move split opinion: UNESCO and many world leaders condemned it, while several Muslim leaders welcomed it.
